title: The Best Models Still Reason Like Toddlers — Andrew Dai, Elorian
talk_summary: A vision-model founder argues frontier models fail at detailed visual reasoning because they pattern-match rather than spatially ground, and pitches visual chain-of-thought and simulation-based validation. The only transferable ideas are general: keep tasks within a model's competence, validate outputs programmatically, and don't trust benchmark scores as proxies for real work.

takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish 'understanding' (answerable in <1s by a human) from 'reasoning' (needs detailed inspection) and show models only reliably do the former; they recommend keeping tasks simple or expecting hallucinations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep these visual tasks very simple otherwise you will have hallucinations a lot

takeaways.what_they_do: They pair model output with simulators and unit-test-like validation ('just like in code, you can run code against unit tests') rather than trusting the model's own answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Just like in code, you can run code against unit tests. You can also run u mechanical devices through simulators

takeaways.what_they_do: They show headline benchmark numbers (ARC-AGI, MMMU) are inflated by toy inputs or answerable without the hard modality, so scores overstate real capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the images are only 32x 32 or 64x 64 pixels

takeaways.what_they_do: They show models lose track of events across long videos ('context amnesia'), missing state changes that occurred mid-sequence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these models can't maintain consistency um across long videos and they very easily lose track of what's happening
